title: Load a trailer in reverse delivery order
instruction: load the parcels into the trailer for the route: the route board shows the stops in delivery order from left to right; the trailer is unloaded from the door, so the first stop's parcels must be nearest the door and the last stop's at the nose
context: Delivery vehicles are loaded in reverse stop order so that each stop's freight is at the door when the truck arrives; loading out of sequence forces the driver to unload and reload at every stop. It measures reading an order from a board and reversing it (last in, first out).
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. An open-topped trailer is fixed in the middle of the bench: a dark floor from x = 14 (the door, open, facing the arms) to x = 41 (the nose), 10 cm wide inside, with 1 cm walls 5 cm tall at the nose and both sides. A white route board (6 x 12 cm) at (20, 30) shows three coloured squares in a row, from left to right: blue (stop 1), red (stop 2), yellow (stop 3). Five cardboard parcels (4 x 6 x 4 cm, 6 cm along y, 80 g), coloured by stop, wait on grey dock mats: yellow at (20, 17), blue at (28, 17), red at (36, 17), blue at (20, -17) and yellow at (28, -17).
scoring: A parcel is loaded when its centre is inside the trailer (between the door line and the nose, between the side walls) and it lies on the floor (underside within 2 cm of it). There are 8 pairs of parcels for different stops (yellow with red 2, yellow with blue 4, red with blue 2). A pair counts when both parcels are loaded and the later stop's parcel lies at least 2 cm (centre to centre) nearer the nose than the earlier stop's. Score = pairs that count / 8; a parcel left out spoils every pair it belongs to. Doing nothing scores 0, and so does loading them in route order (blue at the nose) or loading only one stop's parcels; a yellow at the nose and a blue at the door alone score 0.125; 1.0 when both yellow parcels are deepest, then the red, then both blue nearest the door. Items are judged only by the positions stated above, not by how they are oriented, so one lying on its side counts the same as one standing; anything the rules above don't cover (for example a part dropped off the table) counts neither way unless a penalty above applies to it. On real arms, measure each parcel's distance from the trailer nose with a tape measure (read to ±2 mm), or judge the order from a top-down photo of the end state.
reset_notes: Put the parcels back on the dock mats at their positions.
fidelity: Approximate. The trailer is a small open-topped box at bench scale, and the parcels' stops are shown by their colour, matched to the route board. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Parcels are rigid blocks with rubber-like friction, so they slide less in the trailer than real cardboard.
